newsitem.title: USA: NY Gov. Pataki says Great Lakes pose flood threat.
newsitem.headline: NY Gov. Pataki says Great Lakes pose flood threat.

text.p: New York Gov. George Pataki on Tuesday, saying high water levels in the Great Lakes posed "immediate flood threats" until June, asked the U.S. Army Corps for technical help as a preventive step.

But the governor noted he did not expect New York State, whose western border runs along Lake Erie and whose northern border is partly defined by Lake Ontario, to be struck by the the kind of devastating floods that have hit the Midwest.

"While we can empathize with our neighbors' plight, by requesting assistance from the Corps now, New York State can help local jurisdictions increase their preparedness to protect life and property," he said in prepared remarks.

The water level in Lake Erie is about two feet above average, while Ontario is about a foot over, according to Dennis Michalski, assistant director for community affairs, for the State Emergency Management Office in Albany.

Michalski said the state in 1993 faced a similar situation and took the same sorts of preventive steps, which include getting communities that border the lakes to stock up on sandbags and other supplies
Lowlying communities along the two Great lakes tend to get hit by floods every year, and 1993 was no exception though there was no abnormal flooding, the state official said.
Pataki, in a letter that was released to the media, told Col. Michael Conrad, Commander of the Buffalo Division of Army Corps of Engineers, "Immediate flood threats exist through June of this year."
The governor noted that strong winds could push water levels in the eastern part of Lake Erie over eight feet, and if combined with eight- to 12-foot waves, could cause significant flooding.
He also cautioned that heavy rains predicted for the Great Lakes basin could cause the two lakes to flood through next fall and the spring of 1998.
The Army Corps will helps assess and build temporary restraints that are needed, Pataki said.
